description:
FILED s473c (Opus, 2026-09-08).  PRE-EXISTING: probed identical on main
c2016433 and with #1240's `line-track` gate both on and off.

PROBE (perl 5.40.3 vs PCL):

    eval "die 'x'";  print "[$@]";

    perl  [x at (eval 3) line 1.]
    PCL   [x at - line 1.]

CAUSE: codegen attaches an explicit die's location as a `:loc` marker built
from Pl::Environment's source_file (Pl/ExprToCL.pm, the p-die/p-warn branch).
In EVAL MODE there is no file, so source_file is "-" and the marker reads
"- line 1".  p-die then uses that marker, so the message already ends in a
newline by the time p-eval's error handler sees it, and the handler's
"(eval N) line M" tail is never appended.

A RUNTIME-raised die in the same position is RIGHT once #1240's register is
on -- `eval q{1/0}` reports `at (eval 2) line 1.` exactly as perl does --
because it has no `:loc` and reads the register, which p-eval sets to a
negative file id meaning `(eval N)`.  So the fix is to make the EXPLICIT die
take the same route: emit no `:loc` in eval mode and let the register answer.
That needs the eval-mode fact to reach ExprToCL's die branch (Pl::PExpr
reaches it as `$self->parser->eval_mode`; ExprToCL has no equivalent today),
and it must NOT fire for a program read from STDIN, where perl really does
say `at - line N.`

RESIDUE OF THE SAME FAMILY: a sub DEFINED inside a string eval and called
later reports the CALLER's file, because Parser2::_p_file_form emits nothing
in eval mode (the eval's own `(eval N)` id is set by p-eval around the
EVALUATION, and the sub outlives it).  perl names `(eval N)` there too.
subject: an EXPLICIT `die` inside a string eval reports `at - line 1.` where perl reports `at (eval N) line M.`
